newsitem.title: USA: CSCE world sugar ends quiet session barely changed.
newsitem.headline: CSCE world sugar ends quiet session barely changed.

text.p: CSCE world sugar prices ended barely changed in sluggish dealings Tuesday, as industry activity on both sides of the market confined prices to a narrow range, traders said.
The key March contract lingered near unchanged for most of the session, and in an "inside day" never managed to break through the previous session's trading range.
Scale-down trade buying provided support toward the lower of end of the meager, six-point range, while the upside was capped by producer selling, dealers said.
Traders blamed today's lacklustre market on a shortage of fresh fundamentals.
"Theere's no news, so people aren't anxious to pay up or sell it down," said one broker. "There is good refiner and trade buying, but there is producer pricing from unchanged to the upside."

March delivery fell 0.02 cent per lb on the day, to 10.33 cents, having ranged from 10.32 to 10.38. Second-position May gained 0.02, to 10.44, while the outer months were flat to up 0.01. A scant 5,430 lots changed hands on the day.
Technically, a breach of the 10.29-level basis March could spark some long liquidation, chartists said, while the 10.40-10.50 area loomed as a key upside target.

In the physical market, Syria tendered early Tuesday to buy 13,000 tonnes of each white and raw sugar, but dealers said the news had little impact on the futures market. Offers for the tender were due on November 27, with shipments slated from December 20, 1996, to January 20, 1997.
-- Wendy Pollack, New York Commodities Desk +1 212 859 1640
